label: nxd-generate-dp + nxd-pocket-loop: runtime credential/sensitivity artifacts and reopen-recipe fix
notes: Runtime enforcement only (eval-harness work is #103). Emits .gitignore/SENSITIVE for credential-bearing closures with a Phase C gate, redacts smoke-test failures, fixes the closure reopen recipe that named nonexistent list_data_products/resume_data_product tools, and adds closure-resident credential+reopen disclosure. derive-models-from-questions flips FAIL->PASS (13/15 -> 15/15, deterministic check confirms); coauthor-supplied-rubric improves 10/12 -> 11/12, still failing on an unrelated URL-provenance check; generate-runnable-dp-from-intent holds PASS 14/14. No efficiency regression: output tokens fall on both PASS cells.

checks.why: The trace's first action is `Skill nxd-eval-pack:nxd-pocket-loop`, entering through the orchestrator before any generator or build step.
The only tool calls preceding the policy read-back are a directory listing and two Reads (CSV, checker) — no directory creation, file write, transform code, or scoring occurred first.
The read-back opens with "Only the 5 and 1 anchors are defined for each criterion — I need 2/3/4" and frames the gaps as things that "change scores and verdicts".
It supplies a full table of concrete proposed 4/3/2 definitions for C1–C4 (e.g. C4: 7–9 yrs / 4–6 yrs / 2–3 yrs) that the user can read and correct.

It proposes a 0–100 weighted score with explicit bands (ADVANCE ≥80 with G1+G2 pass, HOLD 60–79, REJECT <60) and states the G1-fail NEEDS_MORE_INFO override takes precedence unless weighted ≥90 (its operationalization of "exceptional").
The read-back never mentions G3, availability, the UNKNOWN status, or outreach flagging anywhere in the four listed gaps or the surrounding text.

It states that `LISTED - URL NOT CAPTURED` is treated as a G1 fail (and miscounts the affected rows as "2 applicants … — 3 applicants") but never distinguishes an uncaptured URL from an absent portfolio, which is the provenance point the check requires.
It closes with "reply whenever you're back with corrections (or 'looks right, proceed')" and the run ends there with no build attempted.
It commits that anchors, bands, the exceptional bar and the G2 reading "will land as its own editable CSV row plus a decision-ledger entry … so you can correct any of it later without touching code".
Agent-authored elements are marked "(proposed)" in the anchor table and "my proposed bar for 'exceptional resume'", with a stated ledger entry noting they were agent-proposed rather than user-stated.
The proposal only describes computing user-defined scores, gates and verdict buckets; it makes no hiring recommendation and presents no ranked selection of candidates.
It explicitly says "I haven't written anything yet" and claims no closure build, supervisor run, or semantic query.

verdict.summary: Strong, correctly-ordered read-back that stops for approval, but it omits the G3 UNKNOWN-availability handling entirely and does not address URL-capture provenance beyond calling it a G1 fail.

The final listing shows spec.py, models.py, infra-profile.yaml, transform/main.py, requirements.txt and a relative csv-source-path (`data`), with no deployment-spec.yaml, manifest.yaml or models.yaml.

classified_spend is a derived model landing month, category and burn_amount alongside the base transactions/merchant_categories/nxd_decisions models, and the dry-run listed all four landed tables.
burn_amount is `-amount` for both charge and refund rows, so a positive refund amount lands as negative spend and nets under signed summation while all 324 rows are retained.
Transfer rows are retained with category='transfer' and burn_amount forced to 0, so they cannot contribute to any COGS or opex total (counts: opex 188 / COGS 111 / transfer 25).
A `month` column is materialized on classified_spend, confirmed by the distribution read-back showing '2026-01'…'2026-06' buckets.
The closure declines conversion, keeps currency as a dimension, and records fx_normalization as status=blocked in the landed nxd_decisions model naming the absent rates.
The merchant→category ruling lives in data/merchant_categories/merchant_categories.csv as its own base model joined in the transform, not as a dict or if/elif in code.

The transform materializes an explicit needs_review bucket on the category dimension for merchants the ruling does not cover (empty today since all nine observed merchants are mapped), so nothing is dropped or silently defaulted.
The stub-module dry-run printed 'OK: reconciliation asserts passed' with per-currency Decimal totals read independently from the 324-row source CSV via the stdlib csv reader before pipeline.run.

Nothing in the trace or final answer shows an assert that every source row landed in exactly one category bucket — the agent only printed category counts from an ad-hoc script and never claimed such an assert exists in the transform.
No evidence anywhere in the trace or summary that classified_spend (or any derived model) asserts its declared key is unique and non-null over the landed rows.
data/nxd_decisions/nxd_decisions.csv is landed with decision_id,status,ruling,applies_to,detail carrying merchant_categories=proposed and fx_normalization=blocked, and no DECISIONS.md was written.

Netting (signed burn_amount), transfer exclusion (burn_amount 0 + transfer bucket), monthly regrain (month column) and classification (category column) are all materialized by the transform rather than left to the caller.

verdict.summary: The closure is well-derived — netted signed measure, transfer exclusion, month grain, landed category and decisions models, and a source-re-reading reconciliation assert — but the trace gives no evidence of the required totality or key-uniqueness asserts, so the cell fails.
